questions.q: During a given month, Ade Ltd recorded taxable credit purchases of ₦400,000 and taxable credit sales of ₦700,000. Assuming an applicable standard VAT rate of $7.5\%$, what is the net VAT payable to (or refundable from) the tax authorities for the month?
questions.explain:
Net VAT is calculated as Output VAT minus Input VAT:

1.  **Output VAT (on sales):** $7.5\% \times ₦700,000 = ₦52,500$
2.  **Input VAT (on purchases):** $7.5\% \times ₦400,000 = ₦30,000$
3.  **Net VAT Remittance:**
    $$\text{Net VAT Payable} = \text{Output VAT} - \text{Input VAT}$$
    $$\text{Net VAT Payable} = ₦52,500 - ₦30,000 = ₦22,500$$

Because Output VAT exceeds Input VAT, the business has a liability of **₦22,500 payable** to the tax authorities.

questions.q: In preparing a VAT return for a tax period, if a registered business has an **Input VAT of ₦45,000** and an **Output VAT of ₦30,000**, what is the final tax position of the firm?
options: The business must remit ₦15,000 to the tax revenue service
The business is entitled to a VAT refund or tax credit of ₦15,000
The ₦15,000 excess is charged directly to the Profit and Loss Account as a business expense
The business must pay the gross Output VAT of ₦30,000 without deducting Input VAT
questions.explain:
When **Input VAT exceeds Output VAT**:
$$\text{Net Position} = \text{Output VAT} - \text{Input VAT} = ₦30,000 - ₦45,000 = -₦15,000$$

A negative result indicates that the business has paid more VAT on its purchases than it collected from customers. The business is legally entitled to a **tax refund** or a **tax credit** of ₦15,000 carried forward to offset future VAT liabilities.
